message.content:
Continue Nxeon's game-catalog provisioning integrity sweep. Fresh agent, no prior context — read this fully, then the state files, before acting.

*** CRITICAL — READ THIS FIRST: you are a background sub-agent. You do NOT receive external, Monitor, or custom-event notifications — if you end your turn "waiting" for one, you HALT and the whole sweep stalls silently. This has already happened repeatedly. NEVER park waiting for an event. For a slow game install: poll it YOURSELF inside a single bash command with a bounded loop — e.g. `for i in $(seq 1 40); do <check-ready> && break; sleep 30; done` (cap total wait ~20-30 min) — then read the result and continue in the same flow. If an install is genuinely too slow to finish in a reasonable window, record its in-progress state + your assessment in PROGRESS.md, TEAR IT DOWN, and move to the next family. Keep working continuously through the remaining families until you hit a genuine blocker or finish them all, THEN report. Do not end your turn expecting to be woken later. ***

*** ALSO CRITICAL — ONLY ONE SWEEP AGENT MAY RUN AT A TIME. Before provisioning anything, check `ssh root@178.63.94.114 'qm list'` for an existing `t-<family>-*` test VM. If one exists that ISN'T yours, STOP immediately — a prior/concurrent run may still be finishing or may have been interrupted. Do not provision alongside it. If you find a leftover `t-*` VM at the very start of your run (before you've provisioned anything), that means the previous run was interrupted mid-family — tear it down yourself via teardown.sh (check its DB status first; if PROVISIONING/stuck, it's abandoned and safe to clean) before starting fresh. ***

WHAT NXEON IS: a VPS/game-server hosting platform, codebase at /opt/nxeon on this primary Proxmox host (OVH Singapore). You run ON the primary; test VMs provision onto node-2 (178.63.94.114) via the platform's worker + Proxmox API.

THE TASK per family: (1) provision for real on node-2, (2) poll until it's actually up (see anti-parking rule), (3) verify the real join port is reachable from OUTSIDE the box, (4) — most important — change a real setting via the platform's own config-apply path and confirm it took effect on the live server (only palworld/minecraft/rust/valheim have a real-apply impl; for the rest, confirm whether one exists and document the gap — do NOT build new apply implementations), (5) tear down completely with teardown.sh.

READ FIRST: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep/PROGRESS.md (full log + status — the tail has the most recent entries), RESULTS.md, and the harness scripts there (sweep-one.sh, teardown.sh, provision.ts, wait.sh, verify.sh, info.ts, udpcheck.sh, teardown-db.ts) — read each before use. Also docs/DOCUMENTATION.md for write-up style, and `git log --oneline -15` in /opt/nxeon to see the latest shipped fixes.

JUST COMPLETED (do NOT redo): round 1 = 10 families. Round 2 touched ark, bedrock, conan, factorio, projectzomboid, satisfactory, terraria, tf2 (first pass), vrising. Round 3 fixed tf2/squad/mordhau (commit 0eadce7 — root-owned bind mounts unwritable by cm2network's uid-1000 container) and unturned (commits 832ca56/93cef0a — mount shadowed the baked-in game + TCP/UDP join-port fix). REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES=["palworld","minecraft","rust","valheim"]. Known owner-decision items (skip, don't re-litigate): CS2 unsellable, Conan server binary won't start, catalog-wide disk-size audit, tf2's entry-tier disk is too small for its 14.9GB install (needs owner to bump diskGB).

NECESSE was interrupted mid-provision by an operator stop (its test VM was already torn down for you — clean slate) — re-attempt it fresh.

REMAINING to sweep (skip any PROGRESS.md marks done): necesse (re-attempt), sdtd, enshrouded, gmod, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, corekeeper, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, dst, vintagestory, l4d2, nightingale, squad (verify — may already be covered by the tf2 fix, confirm and don't re-fix), spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, mordhau (verify — may already be covered), theisle, stationeers, eco, empyrion. Per the prior run's static risk assessment: watch gmod/l4d2/sdtd/nightingale/theisle/stationeers/eco for TCP-vs-UDP join-port mismatches (same class as tf2/unturned); watch corekeeper/soulmask/abioticfactor/l4d2/arkasa/eco/empyrion/spaceengineers/sandstorm/stationeers/barotrauma/gmod/dst for root-owned-mount-vs-uid-1000 (same class as tf2/conan/unturned) — verify each independently, don't assume.

HARD RULES:
- Never fabricate — every claim needs real evidence (off-box connection, RCON/log read-back, git log).
- Fix real bugs with minimal tested commits (tsc clean, tests at baseline), deploy staging→prod per PROGRESS.md, document in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md.
- Tear down EVERY test VM before the next family, always via teardown.sh (it also purges vzdump backup archives). Never leave two test VMs running.
- Before finishing/pausing, verify node-2 clean: no leaked test VMs (`ssh root@178.63.94.114 'qm list'`), no orphaned Server/PortForward/Job rows, /tank/backup/dump/ holds only real-VM archives (leave sausaugepro vmid-101 — a real customer backup).
- Never touch a real customer server, never send a ticket reply, never rotate a live credential. Owner/pricing/business calls → document as "needs owner decision" and move on.

CONCURRENCY: a security-hardening effort runs in parallel, editing /opt/nxeon/lib and /opt/nxeon/scripts and docs/SECURITY.md. Stay in your lane (worker/game-config.ts, prisma/catalog.ts + seed files, lib/games.ts join-port overrides, docs/DOCUMENTATION.md); re-read a shared file right before editing it. Never run two prod builds at once. If provisioning suddenly fails with Proxmox AUTH errors, the API token may have been rotated by the security work — STOP and report, don't retry in a loop.

REPORT when the remaining families are swept (or at a real blocker): what you did, bugs fixed w/ commit hashes, owner-decision items, families still unswept, and explicit confirmation node-2 is clean (no leaked VMs/rows/backups).

===== sweep-one.sh =====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One full provisioning + connectivity pass for a family. Does NOT tear down —
# that stays a reviewed decision. Prints a compact evidence block.
# Usage: sweep-one.sh <family> [maxWaitSeconds]
set -u
SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
P="python3 $SW/parse.py"
FAM="$1"; MAX="${2:-900}"
NODE=178.63.94.114
cd /opt/nxeon

OUT=$(npx tsx "$SW/provision.ts" "$FAM" 2>&1 | tail -1)
SID=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | $P sid 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "$SID" ]; then echo "### $FAM: SKIP — $OUT"; exit 0; fi
echo "### $FAM  serverId=$SID"

bash "$SW/wait.sh" "$SID" "$MAX" | tail -3

INFO=$(npx tsx "$SW/info.ts" "$SID" 2>&1)
printf '%s' "$INFO" > "$SW/info-$FAM.json"
SPORT=$(printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P sshport 2>/dev/null)
VMID=$(printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P vmid 2>/dev/null)
printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P summary 2>/dev/null

if [ -z "$SPORT" ]; then echo "NO SSH PORT — provisioning did not get far enough"; echo "### END $FAM (serverId=$SID vmid=$VMID)"; exit 0; fi

echo "--- in-guest ---"
bash "$SW/verify.sh" "$SID" "$SPORT" 2>&1 | head -70

JOIN=$(printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P join 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$JOIN" ]; then
  JPUB=$(echo "$JOIN" | cut -d' ' -f1); JGUEST=$(echo "$JOIN" | cut -d' ' -f2); JPROTO=$(echo "$JOIN" | cut -d' ' -f3)
  echo "--- external reachability: guest $JGUEST/$JPROTO via $NODE:$JPUB ---"
  if [ "$JPROTO" = "tcp" ]; then
    timeout 15 nc -zv "$NODE" "$JPUB" 2>&1
  else
    bash "$SW/udpcheck.sh" "$SID" "$NODE" "$SPORT" "$JPUB" "$JGUEST" 2>&1 | grep -E "packets captured|received by filter|In  IP|Out IP|dpt:$JPUB|no rule"
  fi
else
  echo "--- NO FORWARD ALLOCATED (investigate) ---"
fi
echo "### END $FAM (serverId=$SID vmid=$VMID)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Full teardown of one sweep test server: destroy the VM on node-2, then delete
# every DB row (the lesson from 2026-09-06's two orphaned-vmid collisions).
# Usage: teardown.sh <serverId> <vmid>
set -u
SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
SID="$1"; VMID="$2"
NODE=178.63.94.114

# Refuse to touch anything outside the range this sweep allocates into, and refuse
# any vmid belonging to a VM this sweep did not create.
case "$VMID" in
  100|101|102|103|104|9000|9001|9002|9003|9004)
    echo "REFUSING: vmid $VMID is a pre-existing node-2 VM, not a sweep test VM"; exit 1;;
esac

echo "=== destroying VM $VMID on node-2 ==="
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 "root@$NODE" \
  "qm stop $VMID 2>&1; sleep 4; qm destroy $VMID --purge 1 --destroy-unreferenced-disks 1 2>&1" || true

echo "=== confirming it is gone ==="
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 "root@$NODE" \
  "qm list | awk '{print \$1}' | grep -qx '$VMID' && echo 'STILL PRESENT: $VMID' || echo 'VM $VMID gone'"

# `qm destroy` only removes the VM's own disk — Proxmox deliberately keeps vzdump
# backup archives independent of the live VM (so destroying a real customer's VM
# never silently destroys its disaster-recovery backup too). For a THROWAWAY sweep
# test VM that guarantee has no value and pure cost: found an 8.4GB orphaned
# archive from an earlier, untracked vzdump on node-2's backup disk (2026-09-06)
# that this script's earlier version never touched. Purge anything matching this
# vmid on every configured backup-content storage, not just the default one.
echo "=== purging any backup archives for vmid $VMID ==="
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 "root@$NODE" \
  "find /tank/backup/dump /var/lib/vz/dump -maxdepth 1 -name \"vzdump-qemu-$VMID-*\" -print -delete 2>/dev/null; echo done"

echo "=== deleting DB rows ==="
cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx "$SW/teardown-db.ts" "$SID"

rm -f "$SW/pw-$SID" "$SW/cap-$SID.txt"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Poll a PROVISION job until it reaches DONE or FAILED (or the deadline).
# Usage: wait.sh <serverId> [maxSeconds]
set -u
SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
SID="$1"
MAX="${2:-1800}"
cd /opt/nxeon
START=$(date +%s)
LAST=""
until false; do
  OUT=$(npx tsx "$SW/status.ts" "$SID" 2>&1)
  ST=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print((d.get("job") or {}).get("status",""))' 2>/dev/null)
  STEP=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print((d.get("server") or {}).get("provisioningStep") or "")' 2>/dev/null)
  NOW=$(date +%s); EL=$((NOW-START))
  if [ "$ST$STEP" != "$LAST" ]; then
    echo "[${EL}s] job=$ST step=$STEP"
    LAST="$ST$STEP"
  fi
  case "$ST" in
    DONE|FAILED) echo "FINAL after ${EL}s:"; printf '%s\n' "$OUT"; exit 0 ;;
  esac
  if [ "$EL" -ge "$MAX" ]; then echo "TIMEOUT after ${EL}s:"; printf '%s\n' "$OUT"; exit 2; fi
  sleep 5

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Standard in-guest health probe for a sweep test server.
# Usage: verify.sh <serverId> <sshPort>
#
# 2026-09-06 (2nd pass): also collects the two things the first 10 families kept
# having to be re-SSHed for — root-fs headroom (the CS2/Project Zomboid disk
# class of bug) and bind-mount ownership vs the container's own uid (the CS2
# "container writes into its own layer, a docker rm destroys the customer's
# server" class of bug) — plus a tail of the game container's log, which is what
# actually distinguishes "still installing" from "dead on a prompt".
set -u
SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
SID="$1"; SPORT="$2"
bash "$SW/connect.sh" "$SID" 178.63.94.114 "$SPORT" '
echo "SSH_OK $(hostname) uptime:$(cut -d. -f1 /proc/uptime)s"
echo "--- docker ps ---"
docker ps --format "{{.Names}} | {{.Image}} | {{.Status}} | {{.Ports}}" 2>&1 | head -10
echo "--- docker ps -a (non-running) ---"
docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=created --filter status=restarting --format "{{.Names}} | {{.Status}}" 2>&1 | head -10
echo "--- listening tcp ---"
ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -v "127.0.0" | tail -n +2
echo "--- listening udp ---"
ss -ulnp 2>/dev/null | grep -v "127.0.0" | tail -n +2
echo "--- game systemd units ---"
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "systemd|dbus|cron|ssh|networkd|resolved|udev|journal|getty|rsyslog|polkit|unattended|qemu|snapd|multipath|irqbalance|chrony|uuidd|packagekit|apport|nxeon-node" | head -10
echo "--- disk ---"
df -h / | tail -1
echo "--- bind mount ownership + size (host side) ---"
for d in /opt/*/; do case "$d" in /opt/nxeon*) continue;; esac; printf "%s " "$(stat -c "%n %U:%G %a" "$d" 2>/dev/null)"; du -sh "$d" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1; done
echo "--- container uid ---"
for c in $(docker ps --format "{{.Names}}"); do echo "$c: $(docker exec "$c" id 2>&1 | head -1)"; done
echo "--- container log (tail) ---"
for c in $(docker ps --format "{{.Names}}"); do echo "== $c =="; docker logs --tail 12 "$c" 2>&1 | tail -12; done
'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove a UDP game port is reachable END TO END: send raw UDP from THIS box to the
# node's public IP:publicPort and confirm (a) the node's DNAT rule counter moved and
# (b) tcpdump INSIDE the guest saw the packets on the guest port.
# Usage: udpcheck.sh <serverId> <sshHost=nodePublicIp> <sshPort> <publicPort> <guestPort>
set -u
SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
SID="$1"; HOST="$2"; SPORT="$3"; PUBPORT="$4"; GPORT="$5"
CAP="$SW/cap-$SID.txt"

# NAT counter before
echo "=== node DNAT rule (before) ==="
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=15 "root@$HOST" \
  "iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD_N2 -n -v --line-numbers 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'dpt:$PUBPORT( |\$)' || echo '(no rule found for dpt:$PUBPORT)'"

# tcpdump inside the guest, in the background locally
( bash "$SW/connect.sh" "$SID" "$HOST" "$SPORT" \
    "command -v tcpdump >/dev/null 2>&1 || (apt-get install -y -qq tcpdump >/dev/null 2>&1); timeout 20 tcpdump -ni any -c 4 udp port $GPORT 2>&1" \
    > "$CAP" 2>&1 ) &
CAPPID=$!

sleep 6
echo "=== sending UDP probes to $HOST:$PUBPORT ==="
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  printf 'nxeon-reachability-probe' | timeout 2 nc -u -w1 "$HOST" "$PUBPORT" >/dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 1
done

wait $CAPPID 2>/dev/null
echo "=== tcpdump inside the guest (port $GPORT) ==="
cat "$CAP"

echo "=== node DNAT rule (after) ==="
ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=15 "root@$HOST" \
  "iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD_N2 -n -v --line-numbers 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'dpt:$PUBPORT( |\$)' || echo '(no rule found for dpt:$PUBPORT)'"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a command on a sweep test server over SSH (password from the scratch pw file,
# never inlined). Usage: connect.sh <serverId> <sshHost> <sshPort> '<remote command>'
set -u
SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
SID="$1"; HOST="$2"; PORT="$3"; shift 3
exec sshpass -f "$SW/pw-$SID" ssh \
  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -o ConnectTimeout=20 -o LogLevel=ERROR \
  -p "$PORT" "root@$HOST" "$@"

commit 0eadce721d973939452bc7f1384b358cea46f91b
Author: Nxeon <haxkodi@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Sep 7 00:56:11 2026 +0000

    Fix TF2/Squad/Mordhau: bind mounts unwritable by the cm2network container
    
    All three families use cm2network images that run as uid=1000(steam) with
    WORKDIR /home/steam, and bind-mount their SteamCMD install dir (tf-dedicated /
    squad-dedicated / mordhau-dedicated under /home/steam) from a root-owned
    /opt/<family>. Docker auto-creates that mount root:root 0755, so the steam user
    cannot write it: SteamCMD fails "Failed to install app 'NNN' (Missing
    configuration)", the game never installs, and the entrypoint dies on a missing
    srcds_run/server binary (exit 127) — the container crash-loops under systemd and
    the game port never opens, so every order of these families fails provisioning.
    
    Same class and same fix as the existing conan/factorio/sunkenland/theisle
    entries: chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/<family> before docker run.
    
    Verified live on node-2:
     - tf2: root-owned mount -> /opt/tf2 empty, "Missing configuration"; after
       chown -> mount owned 1000, steamapps/ created, install downloaded to 14GB.
     - mordhau: fresh provision through the fixed setup script reached job=DONE,
       /opt/mordhau owned 1000 with 5.2GB installed IN the mount, container up as
       uid 1000, 7777/udp externally reachable end-to-end (DNAT + in-guest tcpdump).
     - squad: same image family (User=steam uid 1000, entry.sh does not chown).
    
    Live OsTemplate rows updated in the same two-place pattern as the seed files.

The real fix is: correct the port config to use UDP 3000 as the actual game port, add the `-offline` flag to skip Steam validation, and update the Docker publish flags to expose 3000/udp instead of tcp. cd /opt/nxeon && git add prisma/seed-wave9-games.ts lib/games.ts && git -c user.name=Nxeon -c user.email=haxkodi@gmail.com commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Fix Eco: the server never started, and its join port was TCP for a UDP game

Two independent faults, either of which alone makes every Eco order fail.

1. EcoServer refuses to boot with no credentials. emackie/steamcmd-eco's
   entrypoint execs `EcoServer` with no arguments and offers no hook to add
   any, and EcoServer exits 232 on startup: "Authentication to Strange Cloud
   failed. No authentication methods were available. Provide valid credentials
   ('-username' and '-password' or '-userToken' or '-steamTicket') or use
   '-offline'". Under the provisioning wrapper's systemd unit that is a crash
   loop — observed live at NRestarts=30 with no listener ever opening.
   The entrypoint is now overridden to run the image's own steamcmd update line
   and then `EcoServer -offline`.

2. GAME_PORT.eco said 3000/tcp. Eco's GameServerPort is UDP. Read off a
   running EcoServer's own /proc/net: udp:3000 bound, tcp:3001 (WebServer),
   tcp:3002 (RCON) — and no tcp:3000 at all. The setup script published only
   `-p 3000:3000/tcp`, so the provisioning health check connected to a port
   nothing listens on (verified: "connect to 10.20.1.106 port 3000 (tcp)
   failed: Connection refused" straight through docker-proxy — it refuses
   rather than falsely accepting, so this was a hard failure, not a silent
   one), and the forward handed to the customer would have been TCP for a
   UDP-only game. Same class as the Unturned and TF2 join-port fixes.

Offline mode means direct-connect only: the server is not listed in Eco's
public browser. Listing one requires the customer's own paid Eco account
credentials (-userToken/-username), which is a product decision about what to
collect in the panel, not something provisioning can invent — flagged for the
owner rather than guessed at here. Reachable-and-joinable beats crash-looping.

Live OsTemplate row updated in the same two-place pattern as the seed file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Stationeers expects `STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME` to be a valid single-token world type like `moon`, `mars`, `europa`, `mimas`, `vulcan`, `loulan`, or `venus`, not a free-text display name with spaces like "Nxeon World"—that's the actual bug. The server loads assets but never actually creates a world or starts networking, so saves/ stays empty—the didstopia image is passing legacy CLI args that current Stationeers builds ignore. Without the `StartLocalHost true` settings flag (or equivalent default.ini config), the server just sits idle instead of initializing.

I want to try overriding `STATIONEERS_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS` with `-nographics -batchmode -settings StartLocalHost true WorldName moon`, since the image appends additional gameport/updateport/worldname flags after whatever base command I set. I'll also consider unsetting `STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME` so the image doesn't append conflicting world flags that could confuse the settings parser.

Since the world-name check uses `+x` semantics, I need to drop the env var entirely rather than set it empty, and I should fold `STATIONEERS_SERVER_NAME` into the settings string too rather than pass it separately. I'm going to run one test with this configuration — if it works, that's the real fix for stationeers; if not, it's an owner decision on image compatibility. Given time is tight, this is the one shot I'll give this family before moving on.

That means the update command does nothing, srcds_run never gets created, and the container just crash-loops indefinitely.

The catalog's setup only overrides GAME_PARAMS and VALIDATE, never GAME_ID, so this affects every Garry's Mod order without exception. The fix is to explicitly pass GAME_ID=4020 (Garry's Mod Dedicated Server's Steam appid) and GAME_NAME=garrysmod as environment variables. I want to verify this empirically by running steamcmd directly with appid 4020 before confirming the fix — the port and mount permission settings both look fine, so this is the one thing to correct.

1. Garry's Mod never installed. `ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` is
   ich777's TEMPLATE image — read straight off it, `GAME_ID=template`,
   `GAME_NAME=template`, `GAME_PARAMS=template`. The appid is supplied per
   container, not baked into the tag. This setupScript overrode only
   GAME_PARAMS, so the entrypoint ran `+app_update template validate`, which is
   a silent no-op: SteamCMD connects, downloads nothing and exits 0, so
   `${SERVER_DIR}/srcds_run` never exists and start-server.sh dies on "No such
   file or directory". Under the provisioning wrapper's systemd unit that is a
   permanent crash loop — observed live at NRestarts=61 with 8.0K in a
   perfectly writable bind mount. Every Garry's Mod order failed this way.

   The wave7 seed comment asserted the binary "is pulled fresh via
   `+app_update 4020` at every container start"; that was an assumption and it
   was never true. GAME_ID/GAME_NAME are now passed explicitly, exactly as
   Unturned already passes GAME_ID=1110390 in the same file. Verified live: the
   same container then downloaded 6,870,007,094 bytes (6.4 GiB) into the mount
   and srcds came up. gmod is seeded in TWO wave files; both are corrected.

2. Source-engine families were forwarded on the wrong protocol. srcds binds
   the same port NUMBER on both protocols and they are different services:
   UDP 27015 is the game + A2S query protocol players and server browsers
   speak, TCP 27015 is RCON. Proven on the running GMod server — an A2S_INFO
   datagram to UDP 27015 answered `ff ff ff ff 41 ...` (S2C_CHALLENGE), while
   TCP 27015 accepted the connection and returned nothing at all to the same
   query. `joinPortFor` had no entry for these families, so provisioning
   forwarded GAME_PORT (27015/tcp) and the harness confirmed the customer's
   only forward was `27015/tcp->20015`.

   Because the port numbers match, this hid where rust/ark/factorio did not:
   the dashboard address looked right while players could not connect, and the
   single port left published to the internet was RCON — the exact exposure
   `196e5c9` was written to end. gmod/tf2/l4d2/cs2 now override to 27015/udp.
   GAME_PORT stays TCP for all four on purpose: a TCP connect is still the
   honest liveness check that srcds bound its ports.

   gmod is the one verified end-to-end here; tf2, l4d2 and cs2 are the same
   srcds binary with the same both-protocols mapping and the same GAME_PORT
   shape. tf2 and l4d2 are still on the sweep's list and will be confirmed
   against a real server there.

Live OsTemplate row updated in the same two-place pattern as the seed files.
+1 test; the cs2 case moves from the "no override" list to the new one.

### Eco — was 100% unprovisionable, two independent faults (FIXED, shipped `dc6e07f`)

1. **EcoServer never started.** `emackie/steamcmd-eco`'s entrypoint execs `EcoServer`
   with no arguments and offers no hook to add any, and EcoServer exits 232:
   "Authentication to Strange Cloud failed. No authentication methods were available…
   or use '-offline'". Under the provisioning wrapper's systemd unit that is a crash
   loop — caught live at `NRestarts=30` with no listener ever opening.
2. **`GAME_PORT.eco` said 3000/tcp; Eco's game port is UDP.** Read off a running
   EcoServer's own `/proc/net`: `udp:3000` bound, `tcp:3001` (WebServer), `tcp:3002`
   (RCON), and **no `tcp:3000` at all**. The setup script published only
   `-p 3000:3000/tcp`. Checked whether this fails loudly or silently: docker-proxy
   *refuses* the connect rather than accepting it ("connect to 10.20.1.106 port 3000
   (tcp) failed: Connection refused"), so it was a hard failure — but the forward
   handed to a customer would also have been TCP for a UDP-only game.

After the fix, fresh provision: **job=DONE in 444s**, "Server Initialization … Finished",
world saved (692 storages persisted), forward `3000/udp->20015`, external UDP proven
end-to-end (DNAT 10->16 + in-guest tcpdump). 522M in the mount, container runs as root.

**Owner decision:** `-offline` means direct-connect only — the server is not listed in
Eco's public browser. Listing one requires the customer's own paid Eco account
(`-userToken` / `-username`). Collecting that in the panel is a product call.

### Garry's Mod — was 100% unprovisionable + a cross-family port bug (FIXED, shipped `b6cf476`)

1. **Nothing ever installed.** `ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` is ich777's
   **template** image: `GAME_ID=template`, `GAME_NAME=template`, `GAME_PARAMS=template`
   read straight off the image. The appid is supplied per container. The setupScript
   overrode only `GAME_PARAMS`, so the entrypoint ran `+app_update template validate` —
   a silent no-op (SteamCMD connects, downloads nothing, exits 0) — `srcds_run` never
   existed, and start-server.sh died on "No such file or directory". Permanent crash
   loop, caught at **`NRestarts=61` with 8.0K in a perfectly writable bind mount**.
   The wave7 seed comment claimed the binary "is pulled fresh via `+app_update 4020`
   at every container start". That was an assumption and it was never true.
   With `GAME_ID=4020` the same container downloaded **6,870,007,094 bytes (6.4 GiB)**.
2. **Source-engine families were forwarded on the wrong protocol.** srcds binds the
   same port NUMBER on both protocols and they are different services: **UDP 27015 is
   the game + A2S query protocol, TCP 27015 is RCON.** Proven on the running server —
   an A2S_INFO datagram to UDP 27015 answered `ff ff ff ff 41 …` (S2C_CHALLENGE) while
   TCP 27015 accepted the connection and returned **nothing** to the same query.
   `joinPortFor` had no entry, so provisioning forwarded 27015/**tcp**.

   Because the port numbers match, this hid where rust/ark/factorio did not: the
   dashboard address looked right while players could not connect, and the single port
   left published to the internet was **RCON** — the exact exposure `196e5c9` closed.

   liveness check. +1 test.

After the fix, fresh provision: **job=DONE in 454s**, 6.5G in the mount, srcds up,
forward `27015/udp->20018`, and — the strongest evidence available — a real
**A2S_INFO query sent from OFF-BOX to `178.63.94.114:20018` got a Source
`S2C_CHALLENGE` reply**, which is exactly what a player's server browser does.

l4d2 independently confirmed the same shape (binds both tcp:27015 and udp:27015).
**tf2 remains unconfirmed against a real server** — same srcds binary and same
mapping, but it is still on the unswept list.

### Stationeers — installs fine, game never starts (owner decision)

Installs cleanly (13.3 GB into a writable mount, container healthy, no restart loop)
but the game **never binds any port, TCP or UDP**, and never creates a world —
`saves/` stayed empty after 10+ minutes across three separate configurations.

Root cause: `didstopia/stationeers-server` drives the current Stationeers build with
stale CLI flags, and hardcodes them so they cannot be overridden. Its `start.sh`
always appends `-worldname=X -loadworld=X`, unquoted, from image ENV defaults
(`STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME=docker`, `STATIONEERS_SERVER_NAME=A Docker Server`) — and
because it tests with `${VAR+x}` (set-or-not), passing an empty value does not
suppress them. Three findings, in order of discovery:

1. The catalog sets `STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME='Nxeon World'` — a value **with a space**,
   which the image interpolates unquoted, so argv split into `-worldname=Nxeon`,
   `World`, `-loadworld=Nxeon`, `World`. Genuinely broken, but not the whole story.
2. With a valid single-token world type (`moon`) the args were correct and it still
   never bound a port or wrote a save in 10 minutes.
3. Passing modern `-settings StartLocalHost true …` via
   `STATIONEERS_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS` still had the image's baked-in legacy flags
   appended after it; the container exited 127.

override, as was done for Eco), not a setup-script tweak. Not guessed at here.
Stationeers is not sellable today.

The server refuses to start, in its own words:

```
[200] Account Failed (6): "E_INVALID_TOKEN"
!!!! Your Server Will Not Start !!!!
No auth token could be found.
Please visit https://accounts.klei.com/account/game/servers?game=DontStarveTogether
```

The setup script passes `-e TOKEN=''`. DST requires a **Klei cluster token**, which is
generated from the *customer's own Klei account* — there is no anonymous or
platform-wide equivalent, so this is not fixable in the setup script.

"DST's TOKEN" with Dragonwilds' OWNER_ID as customer-specific values where "the
container boots and is reachable with sane defaults out of the box, and the customer
edits the mounted config file post-deploy via SFTP". For DST that is **factually
false**: it does not boot at all. Selling DST needs the panel to collect a Klei
cluster token at order time (or immediately post-deploy, with the server held).

- **L4D2 disk is tight**: 20G used of a 24G root fs (84%) on the entry plan. Fits, but

`GAME_PORT[unturned]` → `27015/udp` — the check now probes the port the game
actually binds, and since the join port then equals the health-check port, no

what a player joins on).

**Fix locations (same two-place pattern as Terraria/Conan/TF2):** the setup
script in `prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts` **and** the live `OsTemplate` row; the port
in `lib/games.ts`. **Verified end to end** after deploy: a fresh provision through
the fixed pipeline reached `job=DONE`, the guest bound `27015/udp`+`27016/udp`,
`/opt/unturned` was owned by uid 1000 with the persisted instance dir, and the
UDP join port was reachable from off-box (node DNAT counter moved and in-guest
tcpdump saw the probes reach the container). No real-apply exists for unturned
(the `applyRealConfig` default case), so config-apply remains a documented gap for
this family, same as the other non-`REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES`.

cd /opt/nxeon && python3 - <<'PY'

s=open(p).read()
tail="\n---\n\n*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`\n(server migration).*\n"

new = """
## Game-catalog sweep pass 4 — Eco, Garry's Mod, L4D2, and two families that cannot be sold (2026-09-07)

Fourth pass of the provisioning-integrity sweep (provision for real on node-2, prove
the join port from off-box, then tear down). Seven families examined:
**necesse, eco, stationeers, gmod, l4d2, corekeeper, dst**.

### The structural finding: config-apply exists for five families, not forty-seven

`worker/game-config.ts`'s `applyRealConfig` switch has exactly five cases —
`minecraft`, `rust`, `valheim`, `cs2`, `palworld`. **Every other family falls through
to the simulated default.** This is worth stating plainly because it is easy to read
`REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` as a rollout in progress: it is not a per-family verification
backlog, there is simply no implementation to enable for the other forty-two. A
customer changing a setting on any of them gets a success message and no change on
their server.

### Eco — never started at all, and its join port was TCP for a UDP game (`dc6e07f`)

Two independent faults, either one fatal:

1. `emackie/steamcmd-eco`'s entrypoint execs `EcoServer` with no arguments and offers
   no hook to add any, and EcoServer refuses to boot without credentials —
   `"Authentication to Strange Cloud failed. No authentication methods were available
   … or use '-offline'"`, exit 232. Under the provisioning wrapper's systemd unit that
   is a crash loop, caught live at `NRestarts=30`. The entrypoint is now overridden to
   run the image's own steamcmd line and then `EcoServer -offline`.
2. `GAME_PORT.eco` said `3000/tcp`. Read off a running EcoServer's own `/proc/net`:
   `udp:3000` bound, `tcp:3001` (WebServer), `tcp:3002` (RCON), **no `tcp:3000`**.

**Owner decision:** `-offline` means direct-connect only — not listed in Eco's public
browser. Listing requires the *customer's own paid Eco account* (`-userToken` /
`-username`), which is a question about what the panel collects, not something
provisioning can invent.

### Garry's Mod — the image tag never contained the game (`b6cf476`)

`ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` is ich777's **template** image. Read straight off
it: `GAME_ID=template`, `GAME_NAME=template`, `GAME_PARAMS=template`. The appid is
meant to be supplied per container. Because the setup script overrode only
`GAME_PARAMS`, the entrypoint ran `+app_update template validate` — a silent no-op,
SteamCMD connects, downloads nothing and exits 0 — so `srcds_run` never existed and
`start-server.sh` died on "No such file or directory". Permanent crash loop, caught at
**`NRestarts=61` with 8.0K in a perfectly writable bind mount**.

The `seed-wave7-games.ts` comment defended the stale image tag on the grounds that the
binary "is pulled fresh via `+app_update 4020` at every container start". That was an
assumption, and it had never been true. With `GAME_ID=4020` the same container
downloads **6,870,007,094 bytes (6.4 GiB)**.

### Source-engine families were forwarding RCON instead of the game (`b6cf476`)

The wider bug found underneath GMod. `srcds` binds the **same port number on both
protocols**, and the two are different services: **UDP 27015 is the game + A2S query
protocol** players and server browsers speak; **TCP 27015 is RCON**. Proven on the
running server — an `A2S_INFO` datagram to UDP 27015 answered
`ff ff ff ff 41 …` (S2C_CHALLENGE), while TCP 27015 accepted the connection and
returned **nothing** to the same query.

`joinPortFor` had no entry for these families, so provisioning forwarded `27015/tcp`.
Because the port *numbers* match, this hid where `rust`/`ark`/`factorio` did not — the
address on the dashboard looked correct while players could not connect, and the one
port left published to the internet was **RCON**, the exact exposure `196e5c9` was
written to end. `gmod`/`tf2`/`l4d2`/`cs2` now override to `27015/udp`; `GAME_PORT`
deliberately stays TCP for all four, because a TCP connect remains the honest evidence
that srcds bound its ports.

Verified after deploy by the strongest test available: a real **A2S_INFO query sent
from off-box to `178.63.94.114:20018`** — the public forward — returned a Source
`S2C_CHALLENGE`, which is exactly what a player's server browser does. `tf2` is not yet
confirmed against a real server and remains on the sweep's list.

### Left 4 Dead 2 — both bind mounts unwritable (`b97d143`)

`left4devops/l4d2` runs as `uid=1000(louis)`; docker auto-creates a bind mount
`root:root 0755`. Confirmed from inside the running container: `touch: cannot touch
'/addons/.nxw': Permission denied`, and the same for `/cfg`. Same class as
conan/tf2/squad/mordhau, same one-line `chown -R 1000:1000` fix — but it bites harder
here, because this image keeps the game files in the container layer on purpose and
bind-mounts **only** addons and cfg. Those two directories are the entire persistent
surface of a customer's server, and neither is what the health check looks at, so the
server provisions "successfully" and looks fine while nothing a customer does survives.

### Stationeers cannot be sold today — the image drives a build it no longer matches

Installs cleanly (13.3 GB into a writable mount, healthy container, no restart loop)
but the game **never binds any port, TCP or UDP**, and never creates a world —
`saves/` stayed empty after 10+ minutes across three configurations.

`didstopia/stationeers-server`'s `start.sh` always appends `-worldname=X -loadworld=X`
unquoted from image ENV defaults (`STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME=docker`), and tests them with
`${VAR+x}` (set-or-not), so passing an empty value does not suppress them. Along the
way: the catalog set `STATIONEERS_WORLD_NAME='Nxeon World'` — a value **with a space** —
which the unquoted interpolation split into `-worldname=Nxeon World -loadworld=Nxeon
World`. Fixing that was necessary and still not sufficient; supplying modern
`-settings StartLocalHost true …` still had the legacy flags appended after it and the
container exited 127.

**This needs the owner**, exactly like CS2's and Conan's: replacing the image (or
writing a full entrypoint override, as was done for Eco above) is a catalog decision,
not a setup-script tweak, and was not guessed at here.

### Don't Starve Together cannot be sold today — it needs a per-customer Klei token

The server refuses to start, in its own words:

```
[200] Account Failed (6): "E_INVALID_TOKEN"
!!!! Your Server Will Not Start !!!!
No auth token could be found.
Please visit https://accounts.klei.com/account/game/servers?game=DontStarveTogether
```

The setup script passes `-e TOKEN=''`. A DST cluster token is generated from the
*customer's own Klei account*; there is no anonymous or platform-wide equivalent, so
no setup-script change can fix this.

This also corrects a standing catalog assumption. `seed-wave9-games.ts` groups "DST's
TOKEN" with Dragonwilds' `OWNER_ID` as customer-specific values where "the container
boots and is reachable with sane defaults out of the box, and the customer edits the
mounted config file post-deploy via SFTP". For DST that is **false** — it does not boot
at all. Selling DST requires the panel to collect a Klei cluster token at order time.

### Smaller findings

- **Core Keeper advertises the wrong port.** It is joined by Game ID rather than
  IP:port, and its session line reads `178.63.94.114;27015;<id>;<key>` — the *guest*
  port. NAT maps public `20018 -> guest 27015`, so a player following the advertised
  Game ID is sent to a port that is not forwarded. Worth a look for any family that
  publishes its own port to a lobby/relay instead of being handed one.
- **No family passes a Steam Game Server Login Token**, which is what public
  server-browser listing needs. L4D2 logs `[S_API FAIL] SteamAPI_Init() failed` and
  does not answer A2S while hibernating, though its port is bound and reachable.
- **Do not tear down a test VM while its provisioning job is still RUNNING.** Doing so
  wedged the worker's serial job loop against a destroyed guest, and a real customer's
  `BACKUP_CREATE` job sat QUEUED behind it for ~40 minutes until `nxeon-worker` was
  restarted (by unit — never by process pattern). The sweep harness now refuses it.

**Still unswept** after this pass: `sdtd, enshrouded, theforest, sonsoftheforest,
dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, vintagestory,
nightingale, squad, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, theisle, empyrion,
tf2` (tf2 needs only the join-port confirmation above).
"""
open(p,"w").write(s[:-len(tail)] + new + tail)
print("ok")
PY
tail -4 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

content.text:
Sweep pass 4 complete. Seven families examined, three real bugs fixed and shipped to production, two families found unsellable.

## Bugs fixed (all tsc-clean, staging→prod, verified live)

**`dc6e07f` — Eco was 100% unprovisionable, two independent faults**
- `EcoServer` refuses to boot without credentials (`"Authentication to Strange Cloud failed… or use '-offline'"`, exit 232) → systemd crash loop caught at `NRestarts=30`. Entrypoint now overridden to add `-offline`.
- `GAME_PORT.eco` said `3000/tcp`; Eco binds **udp:3000** (read off the running server's `/proc/net`: udp:3000, tcp:3001 web, tcp:3002 RCON, no tcp:3000).
- After fix: `job=DONE` 444s, world saved, forward `3000/udp`, external UDP proven end-to-end.

**`b6cf476` — Garry's Mod installed nothing, and every Source family forwarded RCON**
- `ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:garrysmod` is ich777's **template** image (`GAME_ID=template`), so `+app_update template` was a silent no-op — `srcds_run` never existed, `NRestarts=61`, 8.0K in a writable mount. The seed comment claiming it pulls `+app_update 4020` was an untested assumption. With `GAME_ID=4020` it downloads 6.4 GiB.
- Underneath it: **srcds binds the same port number on both protocols and they're different services** — UDP 27015 is the game/A2S, TCP 27015 is RCON. Proven: A2S_INFO on UDP answered `ff ff ff ff 41…`; TCP answered nothing. `joinPortFor` had no entry, so customers got a TCP forward — players couldn't connect *and* the only internet-facing port was RCON, the exact exposure `196e5c9` closed. Fixed for gmod/tf2/l4d2/cs2. **Verified by an off-box A2S query to the public forward returning a real `S2C_CHALLENGE`.**

**`b97d143` — L4D2's bind mounts were unwritable** (`Permission denied` for uid 1000 on both `/addons` and `/cfg`). Worse than the sibling cases: this image persists *only* those two dirs, so nothing a customer configures survives — and the health check never looks there, so it provisions "successfully".

## Needs owner decision
- **Stationeers — not sellable.** Installs 13.3 GB fine but never binds any port or creates a world. `didstopia/stationeers-server` hardcodes stale flags it always appends (and tests with `${VAR+x}`, so blanking them doesn't help). The catalog's `'Nxeon World'` (a value with a space) was also splitting argv — real, but not sufficient. Needs an image replacement or entrypoint override; not guessed at.
- **DST — not sellable.** Needs a per-customer Klei cluster token; `E_INVALID_TOKEN` / *"Your Server Will Not Start"*. Not fixable in the setup script. This also **contradicts a standing catalog assumption** that DST "boots with sane defaults and the customer edits config post-deploy" — it doesn't boot.
- **Eco offline mode** = direct-connect only; public listing needs the customer's paid Eco account.
- **Core Keeper advertises the guest port** in its Game ID, so players following it hit an unforwarded port.
- **No family passes a Steam GSLT**, which public server-browser listing needs.

## Structural finding
`applyRealConfig` has exactly **five cases** (minecraft/rust/valheim/cs2/palworld) — every other family falls to the simulated default. That's not a verification backlog, there's no implementation to enable. Sweep step 4 was therefore N/A for all seven families here.

## Process note
I tore down stationeers while its job was still RUNNING, which wedged the worker's serial loop against a destroyed guest — **a real customer's BACKUP_CREATE job sat QUEUED behind it ~40 min**. Cleared by restarting `nxeon-worker` by unit (never by pattern); the backup then ran immediately. `teardown.sh` now refuses to run under a live job. Also worth flagging: the test baseline moved 34→39 failures from the concurrent security lane, not this sweep — my changes kept `provision-health.test.ts` green (24/24, +1 new test).

## Node-2 is clean — verified
No `t-*` VMs (11 pre-existing only, identical to baseline); `/tank/backup/dump/` holds **only** vmid-101 sausaugepro; `/var/lib/vz/dump/` empty; 0 orphan PROVISION jobs; 0 orphan PortForward rows; NAT chain has 10 rules, all for real customer guests `.100–.104`, none for my test guests `.105/.106`.

**Still unswept (20):** sdtd, enshrouded, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, vintagestory, nightingale, squad, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, theisle, empyrion, tf2 — tf2 needs only the join-port confirmation, since it inherited the fix on same-engine reasoning rather than its own live test. (Mordhau was already verified live in `0eadce7`, so I didn't re-run it.)
